# Contracts and trust boundaries
Identify callers, input trust, authority and observable failure behavior. Read both sides of a changed interface. Compare declared types and real runtime validation; neither alone proves compatibility or authorization.

For access control, follow the actual identity and resource checks. Do not infer safety from a route name or frontend restriction. For a cross-system contract, inspect serialization, optional fields, version skew, consumers and error handling. Use a concrete failing scenario rather than a list of hypothetical risks.

Keep secrets and production data out of logs and artifacts. Run only authorized tests against safe fixtures. Never alter permissions, authentication policy or external side effects merely to make a check pass.

Return a bounded finding or regression case with source evidence. Sensitive edits need explicit authorization and independent assessment; apparent code size is not a risk measure. A boundary audit covers the named boundary, not a complete security certification.
